title: Durable theory memory identified as a separate sidecar concern
research_question: How can major theory and design rationale survive chat cleanup without making chat or a research diary into project execution truth?
before_state: Important rationale was distributed across chats and historical summaries; the main repository had a broad accepted theory archive but no independent claim/theory/evidence ledger.
result: The accepted main archive preserves a broad historical synthesis. Issue #513 records the PI-approved-in-chat Sidecar design; PR #562 proposes a more explicitly decomposed archaeology archive and D-021 but remains unmerged. The Sidecar is therefore an approved-in-chat design under implementation, not an accepted main-repository decision yet.
key_insights: Research memory must be independent from the execution authority chain.
The sidecar must be non-authoritative, non-blocking, replayable and append-only for historical records.
The two chat archives overlap substantially and should be decomposed into linked records rather than copied verbatim.
The stale PR #514 reference in the accepted archive is recorded here as a pointer correction, not silently rewritten.
negative_findings: PR #562 cannot be treated as accepted main truth while open and unmerged.
A curated seed is not equivalent to a complete replay of all historical chats or commits.

boundaries.source_status: The accepted archive is in main; Issue #513 is open; PR #562 is unmerged and remains review material.
boundaries.implementation_status: Sidecar schema and initial records are being bootstrapped; no automated ingestion is claimed.
boundaries.internal_fidelity: Schema validation is separate from research-content validation.
boundaries.empirical_status: Not applicable to the governance architecture.
